class.name: JarTerrainPopulator
class.description: Base class for things scattered over a [JarVoxelVolume]: where they may appear and how they are placed. Heights are measured from the volume's sea level along its up direction (see [member JarVoxelVolume.up_mode]), so the same rules work on flat worlds and planets of any size. Every rule is a probability rather than a hard cut, so populations thin out naturally: - [b]Rules[/b]: height range and maximum slope, each fading in over a falloff ([member height_falloff], [member slope_falloff]). - [b]Distribution[/b]: a [member mask_noise] fading in around [member mask_threshold] (forests, meadows; [member mask_invert] for the opposite), and clusters: groves of radius [member cluster_radius] about [member cluster_spacing] apart. The density settings are the density where all of these are 1 (inside a forest, at a cluster center). These resources are read from worker threads while populating: change them between populations (see [method JarVoxelVolume.regenerate_population]).

members.member: If [code]true[/code], instances point along the surface normal; otherwise along the volume's up direction (trees grow straight up on slopes).
Radius of a cluster in meters: full density within 60% of it, fading to none at the edge, so features form groves without lone stragglers between them.
Typical distance in meters between cluster centers (one random center per cell of this size). [code]0[/code] disables clustering.
Meters inside the height range over which the probability fades in from 0 to 1. [code]0[/code] gives hard limits.
Range of [member mask_noise] values around [member mask_threshold] over which the probability fades in. [code]0[/code] gives hard edges.
If [code]true[/code], instances are placed where the mask is low instead: e.g. grass in the meadows between forests that use the same noise.

Optional noise that groups instances (forests, meadows): an instance is only placed where the noise, sampled at its position, is at least [member mask_threshold]. The mask is applied after placement, so the density settings are the density inside the areas the mask lets through.
Value of [member mask_noise] (-1 to 1) around which instances fade in. Higher values leave smaller, sparser patches.
Highest height above sea level, in meters, at which instances are placed.
Largest uniform scale of an instance. Each instance gets a random scale between [member minimum_scale] and this.
Steepest ground, in degrees between the surface normal and up, on which instances are placed.
Lowest height above sea level, in meters, at which instances are placed.
Smallest uniform scale of an instance.
If [code]true[/code], each instance is rotated randomly around its up axis.
Meters each instance is pushed into the ground (negative values lift it), e.g. to hide the base of a tree trunk on slopes.
Degrees below [member maximum_slope] over which the probability fades in. [code]0[/code] gives a hard limit.
